issues.description: The template's Farm.singFarmSongVerse method has its Animal parameter commented out (no parameter), while the problem UML and the solution implementation expect a parameter of type Animal. This mismatch can confuse students about the required method signature and prevent them from implementing the verse printing logic that uses the provided Animal instance.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the parameter in the template method signature so it matches the UML and solution: change the method declaration to include an Animal parameter (e.g. private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) { ... }). Ensure the template imports or includes the Animal class so students can implement the method body using the passed animal.

issues.description: The visibility of Farm.singFarmSongVerse differs between artifacts: the UML (and the template) marks the method as private, but the solution implements it as protected. This inconsistency may confuse students about the intended access level for the helper verse method.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the visibility across artifacts. Either change the solution method to private to match the UML and template, or update the UML/template to indicate protected visibility. Prefer making the template and UML consistent with the chosen visibility to avoid student confusion (e.g., use private in both UML and solution if the method is intended as a private helper).
